cases.title: Two shipping labels, no laptop
cases.reportedOutcome: I called my bank that afternoon and submitted the payment receipt, both labels and a cyber-complaint acknowledgement. The bank later told me the receiving account had been restricted while it reviewed the transfer. INR18400 came back in one credit eleven days later. I closed my money-loss complaint after checking the statement; I still do not know who was behind the shop account.

cases.title: A camera deposit before the wedding season
cases.reportedOutcome: My bank has the transaction reference and the complaint acknowledgement. I also sent the marketplace the invoice and the two versions of the video. The listing disappeared, but I have not received the INR7200 or any written confirmation that the recipient account was frozen. The camera-rental expense was separate from the amount I reported as transferred.

cases.title: The drawing tablet and a second clearance fee
cases.reportedOutcome: After I disputed the transfer, my bank credited INR3000 and said the rest was still under review. The messaging platform later told me the sales account had been removed. I have INR6600 outstanding and kept the complaint open. Account removal did not tell me whether the seller used a new account or who actually operated it.

cases.title: The repair desk and a compromised portfolio account
cases.reportedOutcome: The platform acknowledged my recovery request, but access has not been restored. One client confirmed they had not paid the new account. The notification establishes a recovery change, not the legal identity of whoever made it. I kept the incident open.
